indicator.subject: Science
indicator.content_standard: B1.5.3.1: Recognise the impact of science and technology on society
indicator.objective: Identify technologies in the immediate environment and describe the impact of the technology on society

skills.description: Identify technologies in the immediate environment
State what a given technology is used for
Describe a simple impact of technology on society
Explain simply what happens if a technology is absent

misconceptions: Technology only means mobile phones and computers.
Technology has no effect on how people live.
A car or a radio is not technology.
Technology can solve every problem without any human effort.

questions.stem: Which of these is a technology?
questions.explanation: A mobile phone is a technology made by people to help us communicate.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think natural things are technology.

questions.stem: What is a car used for?
options: To travel from place to place
hints: It takes you to school or the market.
questions.explanation: A car is a technology used for transportation.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think cars are for flying.

questions.stem: Which of these is a technology used in the home?
questions.explanation: A television is a technology used in the home for entertainment and information.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think only big machines are technology.

questions.stem: What do we use a radio for?
options: To listen to news and music
questions.explanation: A radio is used for listening to news and music.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think radios are only for music, not news.

questions.stem: How does a mobile phone help us?
options: It helps us talk to people far away
hints: You can talk to someone in another town.
questions.explanation: A mobile phone helps us communicate with people who are far away.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think phones have physical abilities.

questions.stem: Ama wants to travel from Kumasi to Accra. Which technology should she use?
questions.explanation: A car or bus is a technology used to travel between cities.
questions.misconception: Pupils may name household items instead of transport.

questions.stem: How has technology helped farmers?
options: By providing tools like tractors to farm faster
By making crops grow without water
By making the sun shine at night
hints: Think about machines on a farm.
It helps them do work faster.
questions.explanation: Technology has helped farmers by providing tools like tractors that make farming faster and easier.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think technology controls the weather.

questions.stem: Which of these is NOT a technology?
hints: It is found on the ground.
questions.explanation: A stone is a natural object, not a technology. Technology is made by people.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think all objects are technology.

questions.stem: What would happen if there were no cars or buses?
options: It would be harder to travel long distances
hints: How would you get to another town?
questions.explanation: Without cars or buses, travelling long distances would be much harder and slower.
questions.misconception: Pupils may not realize the importance of transport technology.

questions.stem: Kwame wants to take a picture of his family. Which technology should he use?
questions.explanation: A camera is the technology used to take pictures.
questions.misconception: Pupils may confuse the use of a camera with other devices.

questions.stem: Name one technology you can find in your home.
questions.explanation: There are many technologies in the home, such as a television, radio, or mobile phone.
questions.misconception: Pupils may name non-technological items like a chair.

questions.stem: Name one way a mobile phone has changed how people live.
answer: we can talk to people far away
hints: How do you contact your friends?
questions.explanation: Mobile phones have changed how we live by allowing us to communicate easily with people far away.
questions.misconception: Pupils may not see the impact of phones beyond playing games.

questions.stem: How has technology helped doctors and nurses in hospitals?
options: By providing machines to check and treat sick people
By making sick people run faster
By making medicine taste like sweets
hints: Doctors use machines to help patients.
questions.explanation: Technology has helped doctors and nurses by providing medical machines and tools to check and treat patients.
questions.misconception: Pupils may not understand the medical applications of technology.

questions.stem: How did people send messages to others in far places before mobile phones were invented?
options: By sending letters through the post
hints: It took a long time to arrive.
questions.explanation: Before phones, people sent letters by post, which took much longer.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think people always had phones.

questions.stem: Ama says 'Technology only means mobile phones and computers.' Is she right?
options: No, things like cars and radios are also technology
Yes, only phones and computers are technology
hints: Is a car made by people to help us?
questions.explanation: Technology includes any tool or machine made by people to help us, not just phones and computers.
questions.misconception: Pupils often limit technology to digital devices.

questions.stem: Which technology helps us to keep food cold in our homes?
questions.explanation: A fridge is the technology used to keep food cold.
questions.misconception: Pupils may confuse the fridge with other home appliances.

questions.stem: Describe one technology you have seen in your community and explain how it helps people.

criteria.description: Names a valid technology (e.g., trotro, mobile phone, radio)
Explains how it helps (e.g., trotro helps people travel, phone helps communicate)

hints: What do you see in the market?
questions.explanation: This tests identifying technology and its impact in a local context.

questions.stem: Explain what would happen in your community if all mobile phones suddenly stopped working.

criteria.description: States that communication would be difficult
Gives an example of the difficulty (e.g., cannot call for help, cannot do business)

hints: How do people talk to each other?
questions.explanation: Without phones, communication would be much harder, and activities like business and calling for help would be difficult.
questions.misconception: Pupils may not realize how much daily life relies on phones.

questions.stem: Why is it important to learn about technology?
options: To understand how tools help us live and work better
To learn how to break machines
To make our lives more difficult
hints: Learning about it helps us use it well.
questions.explanation: Learning about technology helps us understand how tools and machines make our lives easier and how to use them properly.
questions.misconception: Pupils may not see the value of learning about technology.

questions.stem: Look at a picture of a trotro (minibus) and a mobile phone. Identify which one is used for transport and which is used for communication.

criteria.description: Identifies the mobile phone as communication

questions.explanation: The trotro is used for transport, and the mobile phone is used for communication.
